codes.document_title: ALPA Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Established 1956, revised 2020 for inclusivity. Covers safety, professional conduct, loyalty, leadership, integrity. Professional Standards Committee serves as guardian of the Code.

codes.document_title: IATA Code of Business Conduct
codes.notes: Applies to all IATA employees, subsidiaries, consultants, contractors, suppliers and business partners worldwide. Covers ethical conduct and social responsibilities.

codes.document_title: Professional Air Traffic Controller's Code
codes.notes: Focuses on safety, public trust, and professional excellence. Actions represent the entire profession. Includes Professional Standards Program.

codes.document_title: NATCA Code of Conduct
codes.notes: Anti-discrimination and harassment policy. Covers events, meetings, and professional interactions.

codes.document_title: AFA-CWA Ethical Practices Code
codes.notes: Prohibits officers from receiving compensation from corporate boards or personal payments from employers. Protects members' rights to assemble, vote, and participate.

codes.organization: American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA)
codes.document_title: AIAA Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Covers aerospace professionals broadly. Emphasizes public safety, rejection of bribery/fraud/corruption, crediting others' contributions, fair treatment. Ethics Committee handles violations.

codes.organization: American Association of Private Railroad Car Owners (AAPRCO)
codes.document_title: Code of Ethics & Safety
codes.notes: Private railroad car owners. AAR (Association of American Railroads) focuses on technical standards rather than a formal ethics code. AREMA (American Railway Engineering and Maintenance-of-Way Association) is the other major body.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics for IMO Personnel
codes.notes: UN specialized agency. Code covers integrity, accountability, discrimination, abuse of authority, harassment. Applies to IMO personnel and sets tone for maritime industry.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Voluntary code for maritime professionals worldwide (merchant/naval officers, pilots, Harbour Masters, surveyors, ship managers). Ethical considerations take precedence over commercial interests.

codes.organization: Society of Naval Architects and Marine Engineers (SNAME)
codes.document_title: SNAME Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Follows Professional Engineers Code of Ethics. Covers confidentiality, conflicts of interest, improper solicitation, single-source compensation. Founded for naval architecture and marine engineering professionals.

codes.organization: American Trucking Associations (ATA) - Moving & Storage Conference
codes.document_title: ATA Moving & Storage Conference Code of Ethics
codes.notes: ATA Moving & Storage Conference division code. ATA is the largest national trade association for the trucking industry representing 37,000+ members.

codes.document_title: TIA Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Required for all TIA members and CTB (Certified Transportation Broker) certification. Covers fair dealing, honesty, integrity, professional conduct. Ethics Committee arbitrates disputes.

codes.document_title: USTOA Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Active members must adhere to strict code. Covers truthful representation, accurate pricing, ethical/financial responsibility, professionalism, integrity.

codes.document_title: NTA Code of Ethics and Professional Responsibility
codes.notes: Requires respectful, professional treatment of all, inclusivity. Full code available at NTAonline.com.

subsectors.name: Pipeline Transportation
subsectors.notes: INGAA (Interstate Natural Gas Association of America) and API (American Petroleum Institute) are the main trade bodies. Neither has a prominently published standalone code of ethics for pipeline transportation specifically. API's ethics standards fall under the broader oil/gas sector (NAICS 21).

subsectors.name: Scenic and Sightseeing Transportation
subsectors.notes: Covered indirectly by USTOA and NTA codes under subsector 485. No dedicated scenic/sightseeing transportation ethics code found.

codes.organization: National Customs Brokers & Forwarders Association of America (NCBFAA)
codes.document_title: NCBFAA Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Strict code for customs brokers, freight forwarders, NVOCCs, and ocean transportation intermediaries. Since 1897. 1,400+ member companies.

codes.organization: International Federation of Freight Forwarders Associations (FIATA)
codes.document_title: FIATA Code of Conduct
codes.notes: Covers 40,000 forwarding/logistics firms, 10 million employees in 160 countries. Promotes integrity, transparency, compliance with international trade regulations.

codes.document_title: FAA Order 3750.7B - Ethical Conduct and Financial Disclosure
codes.notes: Regulatory code for FAA employees covering aviation support activities. Implements Ethics in Government Act. Covers financial disclosure and ethical conduct training.

codes.document_title: Standards of Ethical Conduct for USPS Employees (5 CFR 7001)
codes.notes: Supplemental standards of ethical conduct. Covers conflicts of interest, outside employment restrictions, misuse of position. Published in Federal Register 2023.

codes.document_title: Rules of Conduct for Postal Employees (39 CFR Part 447)
codes.notes: Federal regulations governing postal employee conduct. Covers gambling, misuse of position and time, Hatch Act restrictions on political activity.

codes.organization: Association of Couriers and Messageries of Quebec (ACMQ)
codes.document_title: ACMQ Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Founded 1994. Mission to enhance industry image through professional code of ethics. MCAA (Messenger Courier Association of the Americas) is the US/international body but no standalone ethics code found.

codes.document_title: IWLA Standards of Business Ethics (in Bylaws)
codes.notes: Since 1891. Bylaws promote high standard of business ethics for public/contract warehousing and warehouse logistics services. Only trade association for warehouse-based 3PL providers.

subsectors.name: Motion Picture and Sound Recording Industries

codes.organization: SAG-AFTRA (Screen Actors Guild-American Federation of Television and Radio Artists)
codes.document_title: SAG-AFTRA Code of Conduct on Sexual Harassment
codes.notes: Zero-tolerance policy against discrimination and harassment. Part of Four Pillars of Change initiative. Applies to all producers employing SAG-AFTRA members.

codes.document_title: Personal Manager Code of Ethics and Conduct
codes.notes: Governs ethical standards for relationship between performers and managers. Ensures conformity with applicable state laws.

codes.document_title: PGA Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Emphasizes integrity, honesty, professionalism. Includes set safety protocols developed with Hollywood Commission. Anti-harassment training program.

codes.document_title: WGA Code of Conduct / Community Standards
codes.notes: Covers safe, inclusive culture in writers' rooms and professional interactions. Includes Code of Working Rules prohibiting spec work. Agency Code of Conduct also published.

codes.organization: American Society of Business Publication Editors (ASBPE)
codes.document_title: ASBPE Code of Journalism Ethics
codes.notes: Updated February 2025. For business/trade/professional publications. Covers editorial independence, separation of advertising from editorial, transparency. Founded 1964.

codes.document_title: SPJ Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Gold standard of aspirational journalism ethics codes. Four principles: seek truth, minimize harm, act independently, be accountable/transparent. First written 1973, revised 1984/1987/1996/2014.

codes.document_title: RTDNA Code of Ethics
codes.notes: For broadcast and digital journalists. Covers public obligation, error correction, conflicts of interest, editorial independence, diversity of sources. Includes separate Coverage Guidelines.

codes.document_title: Global Charter of Ethics for Journalists
codes.notes: Adopted June 2019 at 30th IFJ World Congress. 16 articles. Completes Bordeaux Declaration (1954). Endorsed by representatives of 500,000+ journalists worldwide.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics for Visual Journalists
codes.notes: For photojournalists and visual journalists. Covers accuracy, resisting manipulation, avoiding stereotyping, treating subjects with dignity, special consideration for vulnerable subjects.

codes.document_title: ONA Social Newsgathering Ethics Code / Build Your Own Ethics Code
codes.notes: Innovative approach: Build Your Own Ethics Code tool for news organizations. Covers 40+ ethical issues including UGC, verification, data journalism, social networks. Also has Social Newsgathering Ethics Code.

codes.document_title: ASNE Statement of Principles (Canons of Journalism)
codes.notes: Originally 'Canons of Journalism' adopted 1922 — landmark document that became model for journalism codes globally. Covers responsibility, freedom of the press, independence, truth/accuracy, impartiality, fair play.

codes.document_title: Consumer Code for Wireless Service
codes.notes: Voluntary code for wireless carriers. Covers service disclosure, mapping, device unlocking. Also has Messaging Principles and Best Practices (updated 2023) covering ethical messaging, opt-in consent, content prohibitions.

codes.document_title: ITU Standards of Conduct / Ethics Framework
codes.notes: UN specialized agency. Ethics Office promotes highest standards. Includes policies on harassment, fraud/corruption, whistleblowing, all updated June 2025. Standards of Conduct for International Civil Service.

codes.document_title: ISOC Code of Conduct for Individual Members / Board and Officer Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Three-tier ethics framework: Individual Members (2003), Board/Officers, and Staff (2015). Covers internet governance professionals. Values: integrity, openness, honesty.

subsectors.name: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting

codes.document_title: ACM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
codes.notes: Gold standard for computing profession. Adopted June 2018 after two-year global consultation. Covers public good, harm avoidance, honesty, fairness, privacy, confidentiality. Applies to all computing professionals.

codes.organization: IEEE (Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers)
codes.document_title: IEEE Code of Ethics
codes.notes: 10 rules covering public safety, competence, fair treatment, discrimination prevention, sustainable development, privacy. All IEEE members agree to abide. Also co-published Software Engineering Code of Ethics with ACM/IEEE-CS.

codes.organization: ISC2 (International Information System Security Certification Consortium)
codes.document_title: ISC2 Code of Ethics / Code of Professional Conduct
codes.notes: Four canons: protect society, act honorably, provide competent service, advance the profession. New Code of Professional Conduct launched Feb 2026 with input from 1,400 cybersecurity professionals. Mandatory for all CISSP holders.

codes.document_title: AITP Code of Ethics and Standards of Conduct
codes.notes: Founded 1951. Three obligations: to society (knowledge dissemination, privacy), to employers (faithful service), to fellow members (honesty, respect). Acquired by CompTIA in 2017, rebranded as CompTIA IT Pro.

codes.document_title: ALA Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Nine principles. Created 1939, most recent amendment 2021 added racial/social justice principle. Covers intellectual freedom, access to information, privacy, professional development, equity.

codes.organization: International Federation of Library Associations and Institutions (IFLA)
codes.document_title: IFLA Code of Ethics for Librarians and Other Information Workers
codes.notes: Approved August 2012. Available in long and short versions. Translated into many languages. Model for 60+ national library association codes. Covers access, privacy, confidentiality.

codes.document_title: SAA Core Values Statement and Code of Ethics
codes.notes: First adopted 1980, revised 1992/2005/2012/2020. Companion document with Core Values. Covers authenticity, integrity, access, privacy, culturally sensitive materials, professional relationships.

codes.organization: Association for Information Science and Technology (ASIS&T)
codes.document_title: ASIS&T Professional Guidelines / Code of Conduct
codes.notes: Covers obligations to employers, clients, system users, the profession, and society. Emphasizes awareness of social, economic, cultural, political impacts. Recently merged with SLA (Special Libraries Association).

codes.document_title: SLA Professional Ethics Guidelines
codes.notes: For special/corporate librarians and information professionals. Merged with ASIS&T in 2025.

key_findings: Air Transportation (481) is the most regulated subsector with 6 codes across pilots, air traffic controllers, flight attendants, and aerospace engineers
Water Transportation (483) has strong international coverage through IMO, Nautical Institute, and SNAME
Broadcasting/Content Providers (516) has the richest ethics landscape with 5 codes including the landmark ASNE Canons of Journalism (1922)
Computing Infrastructure (518) has 4 major professional codes spanning computing (ACM), electrical engineering (IEEE), cybersecurity (ISC2), and IT professionals (AITP)
Libraries/Archives (519) has robust ethics infrastructure from ALA (1939), IFLA (international), SAA, ASIS&T, and SLA
Pipeline Transportation (486) and Scenic/Sightseeing Transportation (487) have no dedicated standalone ethics codes
Several codes are regulatory rather than voluntary: USPS (491) is governed by federal regulation 5 CFR 7001 and 39 CFR 447
The journalism/media codes are the oldest continuously maintained ethics codes, with ASNE Canons dating to 1922 and SPJ to 1973
